body:
## Summary

`fleet-dispatch`'s hand-rolled HTTP response reader does unchecked arithmetic on the peer-declared chunk size in `dechunked_len` — the function `read_response` uses to decide whether a chunked body is complete. A chunk-size line naming one of the two largest `usize` values panics in debug/test builds (`attempt to add with overflow`) and, in release builds where overflow checks are off, wraps so the completeness guard and the slice index are computed from wrapped values. The sibling decoder `dechunk` in the same file guards the same declared size before slicing and handles the identical input safely — the two halves of the chunked reader disagree about whether peer-declared sizes can be trusted.

This is the #5579 rule ("peer-declared sizes are never trusted") applied everywhere else in the fleet HTTP readers — fleet-proxy's `http.rs` caps chunk sizes against `MAX_RESPONSE_BODY_BYTES` with `checked_add` before allocating — but missed in the dispatch client.

## Evidence (verified this run, laptop, origin/main `540d3bea3f`)

`pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-dispatch/src/lib.rs`:

- `:303` — `let size = usize::from_str_radix(size_str.trim().split(';').next()?.trim(), 16).ok()?;` — the chunk size is parsed straight from the response bytes, unbounded.
- `:308` — `if rest.len() < size + 2 { return None; }` — `size + 2` is unchecked: for `size = usize::MAX` or `usize::MAX - 1` this overflows.
- `:311` — `total += size;` — also unchecked.
- `:312` — `rest = &rest[size + 2..];` — slices at the same unchecked expression.
- `read_response` (`:273`, the `complete` closure at `:265-272`) calls `dechunked_len(body)` after every read while filling a chunked body, so the panic/wrap triggers mid-exchange on response bytes alone — no local input needed beyond running `fleet dispatch status|launch|enqueue` against an endpoint that returns such a chunk-size line.
- Contrast `:326` — `dechunk` checks `size == 0 || rest.len() < size` before slicing and never adds to the declared size; and `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-proxy/src/http.rs` `read_chunked`, which does `out.len().checked_add(size)` and refuses anything past `MAX_RESPONSE_BODY_BYTES` before allocating.

### Probe (real crate, laptop worktree `~/git/fleet/probe-dispatch-dechunk-wt` at `540d3bea3f`)

A temporary `#[test]` appended to the crate's own test module, run with `cargo test -p fleet-dispatch probe_dechunked_len_huge_chunk_size -- --nocapture`:

- Control: `dechunked_len(b"4\r\nWiki\r\n5\r\npedia\r\n0\r\n\r\n") == Some(9)` ✔
- Control: `dechunked_len(b"4\r\nWi") == None` ✔
- Control: `dechunk(b"ffffffffffffffff\r\nXX") == []` — the decoder is safe on the same bytes ✔
- `dechunked_len(b"ffffffffffffffff\r\nXX")` → **PANIC** at `crates/fleet-dispatch/src/lib.rs:308:25: attempt to add with overflow`
- `dechunked_len(b"fffffffffffffffe\r\nXX")` → **PANIC** at the same line
- Probe result: `PROBE DONE panics=true true`, test passed (panics caught via `catch_unwind`).

In a release build the same expressions wrap instead of panicking: `size + 2` becomes `1` (for `MAX`) or `0` (for `MAX - 1`), the `:308` guard passes against a 2-byte remainder, `total` wraps, and `rest[size + 2..]` advances by the wrapped index — the completeness verdict for the exchange is then computed from wrapped arithmetic while `dechunk` decodes something else, so the client can finish an exchange early on a body the decoder reads differently.

## Why it matters

`fleet dispatch` is the thin client every seat uses to launch and enqueue sessions through pm-dispatch, over both the direct and the CONNECT-tunnel transports. Its response reader is the one hand-rolled HTTP reader in the fleet workspace that still does raw arithmetic on a peer-declared length. pm-dispatch (Bun.serve) will not emit such a chunk size itself, but the reader's contract — per #5579 and the module's own framing — is that response framing is validated before it is trusted: a buggy, compromised, or mis-proxied endpoint (the tunnel path traverses the egress proxy) turns a status/launch/enqueue call into a client panic in debug builds and a silently wrong completeness verdict in release builds, instead of the crate's normal `DispatchError::Transport` exit-3 path. Panics also bypass the crate's exit-code contract (0/2/3/4) entirely.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `dechunked_len` uses checked arithmetic (e.g. `size.checked_add(2)`, a checked running total, and/or a bound of the declared size against the remaining bytes / the existing 64 MiB body cap) so no peer-declared chunk size can overflow, wrap, or panic in any build profile.
- [ ] A chunk-size line that cannot describe a body within the buffered remainder (including the `usize::MAX` / `usize::MAX - 1` cases) is treated as "not complete" or as a transport error — never as a completed body computed from wrapped values.
- [ ] Unit tests in `fleet-dispatch` pin: the two overflow sizes above, a large-but-plausible size with insufficient bytes (`None`/error, no panic), and the existing happy-path pins (`chunked_bodies_dechunk`) keep passing.
- [ ] `cargo test -p fleet-dispatch` passes on the laptop or in CI.

Scope note: `read_response`'s Content-Length handling and `dechunk` itself are out of scope except where the fix naturally shares a guard; the pooled-connection desync concerns of #5579 do not apply here (one exchange per connection, `Connection: close`).
